## 1. What was read

**1,092 research articles** from 32 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **291** records (21% of the 1,383 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. Every count below is over the full harvest and is inflated by this; the figure above is not.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 549 | 233 | 86 | 496 | 19 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: bioinfo +83%, cancer +25%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). This month is missing *Bioinformatics*. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nucleic Acids Res 376, Nature 122, Science 117, JAMA 115, Blood 63, J Immunother Cancer 56.

## 3. The evidence that moved it

*Written 2026-08-26, at the end of the backfill rather than in the month. These
seven briefings exist to give the later ones a floor, and they are read with the
nineteen-month curve already in hand — which is an advantage the monthly practice
will not have and should not pretend to.*

**Six clinical-stage next-generation checkpoint programmes are running in one
month.** Tiragolumab in phase 1b/2, botensilimab plus balstilimab in phase 1,
a CD47xCD40 bispecific in phase 1, a 4-1BB agonist in phase 1, an NLRP3 agonist
with nivolumab and ipilimumab in phase 1, and DKN-01 in phase 2. Set that against
what the corpus finds later: October 2025 returns **zero** hits for the entire
target list, and across all of 2025 not one *newly nominated* target enters a
phase 1. January is what the class looked like with a pipeline, and it is the
baseline that makes the rest of the year legible. The class did not collapse
under negative trials — the trials it had were already the last of them.

**Foundation models are the single largest block in the month**, and the framing
is institutional rather than technical. A *Nature* perspective
[proposes that cell atlases culminate in foundation models of biology](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39566552/) —
a roadmap in which atlases "are poised to provide" benefits and are "ultimately"
foundation models, with no model built or evaluated in it. Against that sits work
that did build something: a
[foundation model of transcription across human cell types](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39779852/)
and a [tabular foundation model for small data](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39780007/).
The corpus later records skepticism arriving; it is worth seeing what it arrived
against, and worth separating the programme statements from the results, because
counting intent as evidence is the failure this thread is most exposed to.

**Cancer neuroscience opens with a named receptor.**
[39137067](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39137067/) reports a beta2-adrenergic
and NGF neuro-mesenchymal feedforward loop driving colorectal cancer — the axis
already mechanistically specific in the first month of the corpus, nineteen
months before it becomes the healthiest thread in the file.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

Three inversions in the opening month, which is why this thread eventually got
opened. [39601781](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39601781/): targeting CD206+
macrophages *disrupts* an antitumour immune axis.
[39609626](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39609626/): circulating tumour-reactive
KIR+CD8 T cells — effectors by phenotype — suppress antitumour immunity in
patients. [39753140](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39753140/): infiltrating
plasma cells maintain glioblastoma stem cells.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This paragraph counted four, and the fourth was
    [39724910](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39724910/) — antigen presentation
    *by* tumour-associated macrophages driving T cells from progenitor to
    terminal exhaustion. It was read as an inversion because the damage is done
    by an antigen-*presenting* cell, which looks like a reversal of role.

    The thread's claim is about what depletion does, and on that the abstract is
    canonical: "TAM depletion increased frequencies of Tex_prog cells in multiple
    tumor models, increased PETER, and promoted responsiveness to αPD1
    immunotherapy". Depleting a suppressive population improved the antitumour
    outcome. The card now supports the thread. What was novel was the identity of
    the antigen source, not the sign.

[39883445](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39883445/) (*Blood*) summarises CD47
targeting as "many misses; hopeful for a hit" — eighteen months before the phase
3s that end it. The commentary layer knew.

[39641962](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39641962/): colonoscopy outperforms the
new blood tests for colorectal cancer screening. Filed as a refutation on
`interception` in the month the thread opens, which is the correct way for a
thread to start.

### (b) Method credibility

[39549267](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39549267/) (*JAMA*) calls polygenic
risk scores for coronary heart disease an unfulfilled promise of precision
medicine. [39541968](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39541968/) (*Cell*): faecal
microbial *load* is a major determinant of gut microbiome variation and a
confounder for disease associations — which puts a question mark over a decade
of compositional microbiome epidemiology.

[38383604](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38383604/): an annotation
quality-control tool reveals erroneous gene inference across existing genome
annotations. [39673524](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39673524/): CRISPR-based
dissection of miRNA binding sites is hampered by pervasive noise even in isogenic
lines — the first of two miRNA-layer cards, the second being October's finding
that functional targeting happens without seed pairing at all.
